label: Unlinked readings from New Testament, John
summary: 8.58: The before-Abraham contrast has no current report-level consumer. A bridge from the saying to a claim of divine authority needs a defended reading of the first-person formula in this context. 8.59: The reported resort to stones is a reaction. Neither the reason for the reaction nor the intended force of the preceding saying is specified by this clause. 9.8-9: The formerly blind man's ordinary self-identification is a useful lexical control. The case has no Johannine inference from those words alone for it to test.
